title: Discrete de Rham complexes and edge-element foundations

items.title: The real H(curl) graph space on a polyhedron
items.strategy: Define the vector-valued distributional curl, graph norm, and all domain and field conventions.

items.title: Lowest-order Whitney and Nedelec de Rham spaces
items.strategy: Define continuous P1, first-family lowest-order Nedelec, RT0, and cellwise P0 spaces, their orientations, affine transport, and global conformity conventions.

items.title: Zero tangential trace H(curl) space
items.strategy: Define the zero tangential space as the H(curl)-closure of compactly supported smooth vector fields and state the boundary convention.

items.title: Weak curl-free fields on a contractible polyhedron are gradients
items.strategy: Prove local H1 potentials by mollification on balls, glue their constants using null-homotopy of loops, and establish global H1 integrability on the bounded Lipschitz domain.

items.title: Canonical edge moments are not bounded on H(curl)
items.strategy: Use gradients of smooth vertex cutoffs whose H(curl) norms tend to zero while one edge circulation stays equal to one.

items.title: Kernel quotient and gauge for discrete curl-curl
items.strategy: Define the discrete curl kernel, its L2-orthogonal gauge complement, the quotient energy norm, and the multiplier formulation.

items.title: Lowest-order Nedelec edge circulation unisolvence
items.strategy: Show the six oriented edge circulation functionals are dual to the six Whitney edge basis functions on a tetrahedron and verify the local polynomial-space dimension.

items.title: Weak tangential trace on a Lipschitz polyhedron
items.strategy: Define the boundary action on the H1 trace quotient by Green duality, prove lift independence and boundedness, and recover n cross u for smooth fields.

items.title: Whitney edge, face, and cell moments commute with grad, curl, and div
items.strategy: Derive the nodal-to-edge, edge-to-face, and face-to-cell incidence identities from endpoint differences, Stokes, Gauss-Green, and the actual Piola transformations.

items.title: Regular decomposition of zero-tangential H(curl) fields
items.strategy: Build the regular part from a Fourier vector potential of the zero extension of curl u and recover a scalar potential; prove the H1 stability and zero-trace boundary correction on the stated Lipschitz polyhedron.

items.title: Stable mixed curl-curl formulation with kernel gauge
items.strategy: Split the finite-dimensional space into the curl kernel and its L2-orthogonal complement, prove the saddle system is uniquely solvable, and give the exact quotient-energy stability constants.

items.title: Discrete de Rham cohomology and contractible-mesh exactness
items.strategy: Identify local degrees of freedom with finite simplicial cochains, prove the cochain isomorphism, derive exactness for a contractible realization, and state the first and second harmonic quotients for nontrivial topology.

items.title: Uniformly bounded commuting projection for lowest-order Nedelec spaces
items.strategy: Construct a smoothed canonical projection with a boundary correction, prove the correction commutes with the full de Rham differential, and establish mesh-uniform graph-norm bounds and idempotence.

items.title: Discrete compactness and uniform Poincare inequality for Nedelec fields
items.strategy: Use the regular decomposition, commuting projection, topology-aware harmonic projection, and compact H1-to-L2 embedding to prove discrete compactness and the uniform curl Poincare bound on the gauged subspace.

title: Discrete de Rham complexes and edge-element foundations — Examples

items.title: An oriented Nedelec edge circulation on one tetrahedron
items.strategy: Compute a basis edge circulation and its induced oriented face curl flux, including reversal of orientation.

items.title: A nodal curl-free mode outside the compatible gradient image
items.strategy: Exhibit an explicit continuous piecewise-linear vector field with zero curl that is not the gradient of a continuous piecewise-linear scalar, and show why a gauge is required.

items.title: A handle-domain harmonic field with nonzero circulation
items.strategy: On a solid torus, compute an explicit curl-free and divergence-free azimuthal field with zero normal trace and nonzero circulation around the core loop.
